newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel official in London to probe bombs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Israel official in London to probe bombs - paper.

text.p: Israel's Shin Bet secret police chief is in London to investigate claims that last month's double suicide bombing in Jerusalem was carried out by Arab guerrillas based in Britain, the Sunday Telegraph newspaper reported.
It said Shin Bet's Ami Ayalon was consulting with agents of MI5, its British counterpart.
The Telegraph said Ayalon was investigating reports that the suicide bombers entered Israel on British passports and the attack might have been planned by Arabs based in London.
It said Israeli officials found large amounts of Jordanian dinars in the bombers' pockets and believed they received financial aid and training from abroad.
A spokesman for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said he was checking the report.

Another Israeli government official, who spoke on condition that he not be named, could not comment on the newspaper report but said that since the July 30 bombing, in which 16 people including the attackers died, there had been discussion of Moslem militant activity in Europe. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------ISR AELI MILITARY CENSORS MADE DELETIONS FROM THIS REPORT ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
"After the terrorist attack...there was some discussion here about organisations in Europe collecting money for Hamas and Islamic Jihad," the official said.
The militant Hamas and Islamic Jihad movements have waged violent opposition to Israel-PLO interim peace deals, killing scores of Israelis.
The Hamas armed wing claimed responsibility for the double bombing on a Jewish market in a leaflet whose credibility has been questioned by both Israeli and Palestinian officials.
The attackers have yet to be identified.
